paragraphs.source_en: The formal agreement reached in Berlin was an enormous alteration in terms of European intervention; from what has been called "informal imperialism" based on economic and military control to the formalization of the process and direct rule by the governments of Europe. From a European perspective, which was the only one under consideration at the time, such a formalization of their relationship to one another in Africa would prevent wars. It would be much better to focus expansionist inclinations against less well-armed and distant peoples than one's militarily competent neighbours, as the concerned parties were to discover between 1914 and 1918.
